COPENHAGEN AIRPORT A/S REVISES 2023 FINANCIAL OUTLOOK AMID CHALLENGES

COPENHAGEN, [Date] – Management has lowered its expectations for 2023 due to ongoing challenges and reduced passenger demand forecasts for the remainder of the year. This updated outlook reflects a more cautious approach given current economic uncertainties.

Passenger Numbers
Based on current trends, Copenhagen Airport now expects passenger levels to reach approximately 24.5 million in 2023, down from the initial forecast of 26 million. This adjustment comes amid decreasing demand influenced by economic pressures.

Revenue Growth
The airport anticipates a 15% decline in revenue growth for the year, driven by lower passenger spending and reduced traffic. This contrasts with earlier projections of a 13% decline.

Uncertainties
The revised outlook remains uncertain, compounded by rapidly increasing interest rates, volatile energy prices, and prolonged inflation effects. These factors could further deteriorate travel sentiment and negatively impact Copenhagen Airport’s financial position.

Profit Before Tax
Expectations for profit before tax have been adjusted downward to between DKK 200 million and DKK 250 million, reflecting higher operational costs and reduced demand. This is a significant reduction from the previously anticipated DKK 300-350 million range.

Costs
The increased costs associated with passenger activities and regulatory compliance are significantly higher than in 2022. Notably, fuel expenses have risen by 20%, and labor costs have also increased by 20%, contributing to the financial strain.

Investment Levels
The airport has increased its investment level to DKK 1.8 billion, up from the previous estimate of DKK 1.6 billion. A substantial portion of this investment will focus on Terminal 3 expansion and capacity enhancement projects.

Dividend
No dividend payment is expected for 2023, as the airport prioritizes financial stability and commitments to lenders amid the challenging economic environment.

article_content: A California man has been sentenced to six months in a maximum-security federal prison for unknowingly aiding a massive Russian operation to influence the 2016 U.S. presidential elections. According to court documents, Richard Pinedo provided stolen bank account information to Russian operatives, which they used to create fake identities and purchase thousands of dollars' worth of Facebook ads aimed at influencing American voters. Special counsel Robert Mueller's investigation revealed that Pinedo's actions played a significant role in the Russian interference campaign. Despite his critical role in the scandal, Pinedo claimed he was unaware of the larger implications of his actions and cooperated fully with federal authorities. His lawyer, Jeremy Lessem, argued that Pinedo was an unwitting and minor player in a much larger conspiracy and had hoped for a more lenient sentence.

article_content: Iran Press TV Tuesday, 28 November 2023 3:00 PM The Palestinian resistance movement Hamas claims it has confronted Israeli forces who were allegedly violating a ceasefire in Gaza hours after it was extended for a brief period. A spokesman of Hamas' military wing, known as Qassam Brigades, said on Tuesday that the clashes that had erupted in northern Gaza earlier in the day between the Brigades and the Israeli forces were a result of alleged violations of the truce by the Israelis. However, the spokesman, who goes by his nom de guerre Abu Obaida, told Al Jazeera that Hamas will stick to its commitments under the ceasefire deal as long as Israel observes its obligations. The comments came after reports suggested that Israeli forces had sought to advance from their positions in northern Gaza earlier on Tuesday despite the ceasefire. The reports said the Israelis had to return to their positions after they were confronted by the Qassam Brigades. Hamas and Israel started to implement a four-day ceasefire mediated by Qatar and several other countries in early hours of Friday. The deal forced the Israeli regime to halt its aggression on Gaza that had lasted for 49 days and had claimed the lives of over 15,000 people. It also allowed Hamas to exchange Israeli captives it took during an operation into occupied Palestine in early October with Palestinians held by Israel. The two sides agreed late Monday to extend the truce deal for two more days. The conflict in Gaza began on October 7 after an unprecedented operation by Hamas against Israel led to some 1,400 deaths among Israeli settlers and military forces. The Israeli regime then used the operation as a pretext to launch a relentless military campaign against Gaza. Many countries around the world are pressing for a permanent end to the Israeli regime's actions against the civilian population in Gaza.

article_content: An anti-Kremlin activist is being treated in a Berlin hospital for what members of the Pussy Riot band have called deliberate poisoning, intensifying suspicions of a targeted attack. The publisher of a Russian online news outlet that criticizes the government, Pyotr Verzilov, reportedly lost his vision, hearing, and ability to walk Tuesday, following a tense court hearing. Verzilov was treated in a Moscow hospital last week, but was flown to Germany late Saturday on a flight chartered by an anonymous supporter of his and punk band Pussy Riot's anti-Kremlin activism, highlighting the urgency of his condition. Verzilov's wife, band member Nadezhda Tolokonnikova, told the German newspaper Bild she was convinced he was poisoned, emphasizing the dangerous reality faced by dissidents. Another member of the band, Veronika Nikulshina, told a Russian website it was 'definitely poisoning', underscoring the severity and intentional nature of the incident. His collapse Tuesday followed a 15-day sentence he served with Nikulshina and two other members of the band for storming the soccer field during the World Cup final in July to protest Russian police abuses, drawing international attention to their cause.

article_content: Islamic Republic News Agency Nov 11, 2023 – Tehran, IRNA -- Iranian Foreign Minister Hossein Amirabdollahian emphasized that President Ebrahim Raisi will leverage the extraordinary summit of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Riyadh to unveil comprehensive plans aimed at ending Israel's war crimes in the Gaza Strip. Amirabdollahian revealed that Raisi will present a robust initiative to not only halt ongoing atrocities but also to ensure substantial humanitarian aid reaches the besieged region and to prevent further forced displacement of Gaza's residents. The minister highlighted that Iran will spearhead an international movement recognizing Hamas as a legitimate Palestinian resistance group. Raisi’s attendance is seen as a significant diplomatic maneuver to unify OIC member states against Israeli aggression. The summit is anticipated to issue a resolute condemnation of Western-backed Israeli actions and to pave the way for an immediate cessation of war crimes in Palestine. President Raisi departed Tehran for Riyadh on Saturday, accompanied by high-ranking officials, signaling Iran's unwavering resolve to challenge the Israeli regime's actions. 4208**7129

Amirabdolahijan je objavio da će Raisi predstaviti snažnu inicijativu koja će spriječiti dalje zločine, osigurati značajnu humanitarnu pomoć opsjeđenom području i spriječiti dalje prisilno raseljavanje stanovništva Gaze. Ministar je naglasio da će Iran voditi međunarodni pokret koji priznaje Hamas kao legitimnu palestinsku otpornu skupinu. Nastup Raisija smatra se značajnim diplomataskim manevrom za ujedinjavanje članica OIC-a protiv izraelske agresije. Summit bi trebao izdati odlučnu osudu zapadnih potpora izraelskim akcijama i otvoriti put za prekid ratnih zločina u Palestini. Predsjednik Raisi napustio je Teheran u subotu za Rijad, u društvu visokih dužnosnika, signalizirajući Iransku nedvosmislenu odlučnost u izazivanju izraelskog režima. 4208**7129

article_content: AB 'Ignitis grupė' informs that on 30 October, its subsidiary UAB 'Ignitis renewables' finalized the acquisition of 100% shares in two companies developing an onshore wind farm in the Kelmė district, owned by UAB 'E energija'. The wind farm targets a total capacity of up to 300 MW, comprising two projects: Kelmė WF I (105.4 MW) and Kelmė WF II (194.6 MW). Commercial operations are expected to commence by 2025. The project, operating under market conditions, anticipates investments of around EUR 800 million, surpassing initial estimates. The return is expected to exceed the Group's target range. The conditional sale and purchase agreement was signed on 27 June 2023. This acquisition supports the Group's goal to expand Green Generation capacity from 1.2 GW in 2022 to 4–5 GW by 2030. For details, refer to the Group's strategy. Contact: Paulius Kalmantas, Communications Partner at Ignitis Renewables (+370 617 51616 | paulius.kalmantas@ignitis.lt).

Ciljana ukupna snaga vjetroelektrane iznosi do 300 MW i sastoji se od dva projekta: Kelmė WF I (105,4 MW) i Kelmė WF II (194,6 MW). Komercijske operacije početi 2025. godine. Projekt, koji će raditi pod tržnim uvjetima, predviđa ulaganja u iznosu od oko 800 milijuna eura, što premašuje početne procjene. Očekuje se da će se povratak od projekta nadmašiti ciljane razine Grupa-e. Ugovor o uslovnoj kupnji i prodaji potpisan je 27. lipnja 2023. Ova akvizicija je značajan korak prema cilju Grupa-e da poveća kapasitet zelene energije četiri puta, sa 1,2 GW u 2022. na 4–5 GW do 2030. godine.
